title: Muji Still — Unbleached Object Study
description: A single household object rests centered on unbleached beige, flanked by deep margin silence, with stacked bilingual captions and a hairline rule doing the work that bold type refuses to do.
philosophy: This template is built on Kenya Hara's principle that emptiness is not absence but content — the margins are the message, not its container. It refuses bold weights, decorative color, and any element that competes with the object being shown. The bilingual caption stack treats language itself as a quiet design material, using size and spacing alone to establish reading order. It exists for speakers who believe that a brand confident enough to show less earns more trust than one that fills every corner.
goodFor: Single-product lifestyle launches for household or stationery brands
Bilingual (EN/JP or EN/KR) audience product reveals
Brand decks where editorial restraint is the premium signal
Caption-only interstitial slides within a longer minimalist narrative
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly reviews requiring bold data labels and callouts
High-energy promotional countdowns or sales-urgency pitches
Multi-product comparison grids with dense specification text
Audiences expecting visual drama, motion, or layered typographic hierarchy
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a Japanese design catalog page where silence is the signature — still, unadorned, confident in what it withholds. The central object floats in unbleached calm; surrounding negative space functions as active composition, not leftover void. A hairline rule and scale contrast alone establish reading order from primary to secondary language in the bilingual caption stack. Avoid decorative flourishes, weight-based hierarchy, or any competing element that disrupts the object's quiet centrality.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a generous outer margin (~10%) on all sides; the hero object is centered within cols 5–8 and occupies the upper-center third of the canvas. Title and subtitle stack left-aligned below the object in cols 4–9, divided from the object by a single hairline rule. Bilingual caption pair follows immediately — primary language at reading size, secondary noticeably smaller, sharing the same left edge. No header band; a discreet folio sits bottom-right outside the content grid.

examples.promptCore: Feels like a spread from a Muji catalog — clinical stillness around a single quietly dignified object resting on warm unbleached ground. The composition breathes asymmetrically: the negative field above the object is treated as active material, not wasted space. The bilingual caption stack below the hairline reads like a museum placard — unhurried, bilateral, trusting the reader to close the distance. Avoid any decorative flourish, gradient, shadow, or weight contrast that would compete with the object's plainness.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with deep bilateral margins at roughly 15% each side, concentrating the object study within a centered 6-column island. A single hairline rule divides the object zone from the bilingual caption stack below — primary-language caption left-aligned first, secondary-language caption at a visibly smaller size with generous line gap beneath it. No header band; a discreet page number anchors the bottom-right corner within the outer margin silence. All content is weighted toward the lower half of the canvas, preserving the upper field as pure negative space.
